extracted.intended_audience: writers participating in or considering entering the NYC Midnight Short Story Challenge (2026)
extracted.subtask_description: A four-round, assignment-based timed short-story competition where writers are randomly grouped, receive specific genre/subject/character assignments, and must submit original stories within strict word- and time-limits; judges choose top finishers to advance and provide feedback for every submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment requirements (genre, subject, character)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers are placed randomly in groups and are assigned a genre, subject, and character assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories must be written to the provided assignments for that round (genre, subject, and character). Assignments are central to the challenge format and change each round; failing to follow the assignment would not meet the competition requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have eight days to write an original story no longer than 2,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each submission must be an original story created for the challenge (i.e., not previously published or submitted elsewhere). The phrase 'original story' is used explicitly for the 1st Round and applies to submissions throughout the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1st Round word count limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1st Round submission must not exceed 2,000 words. Exceeding the stated word count would violate the official entry constraints for that round.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2nd Round word count limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers advancing to the 2nd Round must submit stories of 1,750 words or fewer within the round's constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3rd Round word count limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers advancing to the 3rd Round must submit stories of 1,500 words or fewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Round word count limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalists must submit a story of 1,250 words or fewer within the final round's time constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1st Round time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have eight days to write their 1st Round story (January 23-31, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1st Round provides an eight-day window in which to compose and submit the assigned original story; deadlines are enforced and a countdown is provided on the assignments page.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2nd Round time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have three days to write their 2nd Round story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2nd Round is time-compressed (three days) compared with the 1st Round; authors must complete the assigned story within that window.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3rd Round time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have two days to write their 3rd Round story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 3rd Round reduces the time further to two days; authors must adhere to this submission window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Round time limit (24-hour challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final round writers are challenged to write a story no longer than 1,250 words in just 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final round is a single 24‑hour timed sprint; submissions must be completed and uploaded within that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group placement and advancement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers are placed randomly in groups; the judges choose a top five in each group to advance to the next round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advancement is determined by judges’ selections (top five per group). Random group assignment means competition is against a small cohort each round rather than the entire entrant pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges select finalists and winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges select finalists (and winners) through the multi-round judging process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalists are chosen by judges after the 3rd Round and Final Round; the page emphasizes judge-driven selection without detailing scoring rubrics, so entrants should meet assignments and deadlines and rely on judge feedback and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback provided for every submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback from the judges is provided for every submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every author receives judge feedback on their submission, which is a key feature of the contest and a principal learning benefit regardless of advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review forum availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A special review forum is available for the participants to submit their stories for review from fellow writers throughout the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants may use the community forum to get additional peer feedback beyond judge comments; the forums are described as welcoming and helpful for writers of all levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and upload process
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition pages include a countdown to the submission deadline and details on how to upload the stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers must follow the stated upload instructions and meet the posted deadlines. The site recommends marking calendars and notes that contest emails can go to junk/spam, so entrants should proactively track round start and end times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fee donation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Two percent of each entry fee will be donated to charities, and writers can choose where their donation goes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation includes a paid entry fee of which 2% is donated; entrants are given the option to select the beneficiary charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional discount for social media post
rubrics_metrics.description: Get $10 off the entry fee just for posting to social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest offers a $10 promotional code to writers who make a specified social media post; details and link provided on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights retention by writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers retain all the rights to the stories they create during the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contest explicitly states that authors keep all rights and that the organizers will not share stories publicly without the authors' consent; entrants should expect to maintain full copyright control.
